claims.statement: The FastAPI application composes dashboard, plan, workflow approval, Linear, Slack, GitHub, Notion, and health/completion routers; it validates CORS configuration to reject wildcard origins when credentials are enabled, and its lifespan startup validates sandbox provider and local-development LLM model configuration before serving.
GitHub, Linear, and Slack webhook routes verify their platform signature against the raw request body before JSON parsing and return HTTP 401 when verification fails.
Slack message delivery is deduplicated by claiming the event id before the normal background task is scheduled, so only a claimed event can create a Slack run.
Slack blocks operations in externally shared or unverified channels; an app mention in an external shared channel receives a claimed one-time refusal reply and is not dispatched.
Outside code channels, Slack only admits ordinary messages directed at Open SWE through a mention, DM, ready-plan reply, or qualifying untagged two-party reply, and it drops bot/self messages.
Slack resolves a location by preferring an explicit mapping, then metadata matches, then a deterministic id; a conflicting explicit mapping is surfaced as an error rather than guessed.
Slack processing requires a valid mapped user GitHub token unless bot-token-only mode is enabled, and prompts the user to link or re-authenticate instead of dispatching when the token is unavailable.
Slack sends explicit requests with multitask_strategy='interrupt' and other follow-ups with 'enqueue'; message edits are queued rather than dispatched as standalone runs.

Linear accepts only non-bot Comment create events mentioning Open SWE, resolves a repository from explicit comment text, user default, team/project mapping, or team default, and rejects a result outside the allowlist.

A Linear worker reacts to the triggering comment, derives the thread from the issue id, records Linear issue context, serializes the issue and comments into typed input, dispatches it, and posts a trace comment.

GitHub routes multiplex issue, PR, comment, review, push, and CI events, filter unsupported actions, apply repository/organization gates, require mentions for ordinary issue/comment work, and route review-finding replies separately.

GitHub PR comment processing recovers an embedded Open SWE branch UUID when present and otherwise derives a PR thread id, resolves the user's token with one 401 refresh retry, reacts with eyes, serializes comments since the last tag, and dispatches them.
Reviewer runs use reviewer_thread_id and assistant_id='reviewer', separating auto-review and re-review work from the coding-agent thread and graph.

The dashboard allows lazy creation only for run.start, enriches it with authenticated-user attribution, normalized configuration and structured input, while active-thread dashboard messages are queued and cancellation interrupts all live runs on the thread.

Desktop execution happens through a bridge (sandbox) bound to a thread; a thread can be moved to a machine running the desktop CLI via worktree handoff, after which downstream execution validates only allowlisted local projects or worktrees under the configured root are accessed.
Schedules are represented by LangGraph crons; a schedule tick creates a fresh UUID thread after obtaining schedule/automation metadata and rechecking the creator's repository access.
Thread-id derivations are a persisted cross-process routing contract, so changing their namespaces or input strings can orphan live threads.

Input serialization enforces human/system kind alignment, XML-escapes authored content in input-message envelopes, and uses SHA-256-hashed dynamic context introductions with untrusted channel topic/purpose fields marked trust='untrusted'.
dispatch_agent_run rejects mixing a prebuilt input with raw content or identities, otherwise constructs input as needed and delegates all agent/reviewer triggers to create_durable_run.

create_durable_run defaults to interrupt multitasking, async durability, resumable streaming, Protocol v3 stream configuration and subgraphs via V3_RUN_STREAM_MODES, and correlates configurable state and metadata with invocation_id (legacy prepare_run_id).
A completion webhook is attached only when its secret is configured and its URL is absolute and non-loopback; the receiving health route fails closed on the token.

Run completion schedules eligible successful Slack cost refreshes and, for error or timeout, performs best-effort reviewer/code-channel cleanup and source-specific failure replies with per-run idempotence; interrupted runs are not failure replies.
RunInput is a TypedDict carrying messages and optional files, where messages are structured XML-escaped envelopes with sender identity, surface, kind, channel context, and authored content.

invocation_id is generated via new_invocation_id() as a UUID and tracked in both configurable['invocation_id'] and metadata['invocation_id'], with legacy prepare_run_id aliases, used for webhook delivery deduplication and run lifecycle correlation.
RunMetadata records pull_request for reviewer/review-scout graphs to track which PR review page shows the run; start and end invalidate the PR's dashboard widget.

RunConfig assembly by prepare_run_config merges caller-provided config/metadata, resolves or creates invocation_id, sets invocation_started_at, marks v3 streaming via __event_streaming_v2, and preserves unknown keys for forward compatibility.

The v3 streaming protocol is enabled on every durable run via __event_streaming_v2=True in configurable, stream_mode list with values/updates/messages/custom/tasks/checkpoints, and stream_subgraphs=True, allowing dashboard replay and nested-agent visibility.

Scheduled agent runs create fresh UUID threads, obtain schedule/automation metadata, recheck creator repository access, and optionally establish Slack root messages for status replies when configured.

Dashboard run.start commands attribute work to the authenticated GitHub user, resolve model/effort from team/profile/request overrides, validate images for type/count/size/model-capability, and replace raw messages with typed web input.
Bridge tool results are buffered at the desktop CLI and later read during run reconnection, enabling stateless cloud-to-desktop execution coordination.
Resumed runs on interruption preserve full message history and checkpoint state from the halted run, allowing the agent to resume reasoning with prior context intact.
LinearIssueRef, SlackThreadRef, and NotionPageRef source context objects live in RunConfig configurable state, allowing runs to find and recall their originating external platform thread/issue.
